description: Turn object/person detection into TouchDesigner control channels — with NO CUDA requirement. Two backends: 'websocket' subscribes to an external detector process that streams JSON detections over a WebSocket (runs on any machine/GPU, or none), and 'onnx' scaffolds a CPU Script CHOP that runs an .onnx model via onnxruntime inside TD. Either way the output is a Null CHOP carrying a stable contract — presence (0/1), count, and per-object normalized bboxes (obj1_x, obj1_y, obj1_w, obj1_h, obj1_score, …) — ready for bind_to_channel. (Detection idea inspired by TDYolo, MIT-licensed; no code copied.)

input_top.description: (onnx) Absolute path of the TOP to read frames from for inference. Pulled via a Select TOP.

max_objects.description: Number of detected objects (bboxes) to expose as channels (obj1_x, obj1_y, …).

model_path.description: (onnx) Filesystem path to the .onnx model to load in the Script CHOP (CPU inference).

name.description: Base name for the container COMP.

parent_path.description: COMP to create the detection container in (default '/project1').

reconnect_seconds.description: (websocket) Auto-reconnect interval if the detector connection drops.

source.description: Detector backend. 'websocket' subscribes to an external detector process that streams JSON detections (no CUDA needed, runs anywhere). 'onnx' scaffolds a Script CHOP that runs an ONNX model via onnxruntime on the CPU inside TouchDesigner — you fill in the model path + inference.

url.description: (websocket) URL of the external detector's WebSocket. It should send JSON objects like {"count": N, "objects": [{"x":..,"y":..,"w":..,"h":..,"score":..}]}.
